title: Derived Hom and object descent for a normalized native functor
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime and $X$ a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible in every local ring. Let $D$ be a normalized native functor of [def-sf-locally-finite-adic-normalized-functor]. For every two source objects $K,L$, its map from $\operatorname{Hom}(K,L)$ to the full ambient derived $\operatorname{Hom}(D.JK,D.JL)$ is bijective. For every native derived object $M$, bounded adic constructibility in the sense of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework] holds if and only if $M$ is isomorphic to $D.JA$ for some source object $A$. This proves properties of the given functor and does not construct its coefficient maps or comparisons.

source.place: Native realization proof step 3 (constructibility comparison) and steps 6--7 (Hom and object descent).

proof.text: Apply the independently established Hom descent and essential-image descent clauses to the given normalized functor and combine them into the stated conjunction.
